## Body

ROUND 1 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:325
Head: 9a77968f9528cd7cd099e4fcb5693e745b0f1a2d
Answers: 01a1fef6-140b-77c2-86e0-ea2961c644b5

No new periodic worker, per-seat launch, process probe or launch site is added. The alarm reuses the existing death sweep and ordinary PA delivery; the Copilot change adds one environment assignment to existing launches/version inspection. No demonstrated normal-use resource-cost breach blocks this head. The cost row needs more precise deque, role-join and alarm-rate accounting.

Verified cost:
| Path | Work and scaling |
|---|---|
| Death sweep counting | Existing default5s sweep (PIJ_RS_DEATH_SWEEP_MS can change it); one synchronous mutex around observe, never across an await. With W previous window retirements and R new retirements, VecDeque::retain tests W timestamps, then extend clones R seat IDs: O(W+R) per sweep. No per-live-seat counting work is added to the existing reaper. |
| Quiet sweeps / memory | R=0 does NOT mean zero work while W>0: retain still walks the window. At default cadence, nominal0.2 window traversals/s. With an empty window, only constant overhead remains. Stored entries are retirements, not distinct current seats: re-retiring a revived ID can add another entry. IDs age out against the60s observation window; there is no hard numerical/byte cap or explicit capacity shrink. |
| Alarm preparation | When triggered, clone all W window seat IDs, count harnesses and serialize every ID into death.mass. The PA text lists at most20 IDs, but the event and internal alarm do not. Memory/serialization are O(W), not bounded by the display limit. |
| PA discovery | One live-registry list plus one persisted-role list, each with its schema check. join_roles loads A assignment rows into a BTreeMap and removes roles for N live descriptors: O(A log A + N log A) bookkeeping, not merely a constant PA lookup. The role query reads all persisted seat_roles, not just the P current PAs. |
| PA fan-out | P serial wake_pa calls, one per watched live PA. Each includes the existing cold-check reads, a conditional forced-cold-wake audit write, and ordinary delivery admission/queue/outcome work. Body cloning is O(P * body bytes). One additional death.mass publication follows with its own spine transaction/broadcast. An intentional PA wake can cause harness/model work; zero new daemon launch sites is not a zero-cost PA turn. |
| Rate | last_alarm_at suppresses alarms until the sampled now_ms advances by60,000ms, within this daemon's in-memory state. Under a normal advancing wall clock, about one fan-out batch/minute, hence P wake attempts/minute. It is not a server-global or unconditional monotonic delivery-rate ceiling: a restart forgets the cooldown/window, wall-clock jumps affect it, and now_ms is sampled before sweep/obituary/PA work. A slow sweep can compress the later actual notification times. No extra retry timer is introduced when a PA/audit/event write fails. |
| F271c | Spawn/resume plans append COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false before the existing Copilot executable; non-Copilot plans are unchanged. installedVersion still starts one copilot --version per invocation, now with the same flag plus its existing offline flag. No extra version probe, daemon tick or process launch is added. A direct niced helper run resolved1.0.115-5. No updater/plugin-download saving or installed-binary contract guarantee was measured by this performance review. |

Sources: death_sweep.rs:43-62,93-128,138-151,154-242,280-285; http/role.rs:262-274; store/orchestration.rs:323-332; pa_watchdog.rs:331-369,391-431; harnesses/spawn.rs:193-204; harness/scripts/copilot-cli.mjs:10-17.
